issues.body: `assert_report_seam` tokenizes the entire `run:` body, checks that `python3` immediately precedes the script token, and checks only the tokens after the script. It does not constrain tokens before `python3` beyond requiring a separate `set -euo pipefail` line. Thus a body such as `set -euo pipefail\ntrue || python3 scripts/gate-staleness.py --head-sha "$PR_HEAD_SHA" --base-ref "$PR_BASE_REF"` passes every assertion: the invocation and exact argv are present, there is no YAML `if:`, and the required shell option line exists, but `true ||` prevents the reporter from ever running. The mutant table tests YAML-level `if: false` but no non-crashing shell-level inert form, so the self-test remains green. This defeats the module's stated structural defense against an always-zero advisory becoming silent.
issues.fix_hint: Parse and require the live command as an exact executable command line (for example, exactly two nonblank shell lines: the exact `set -euo pipefail` line and the exact `python3 ...` invocation), or otherwise reject shell control operators/prefixes around it. Add a non-crashing mutant such as `true || <invocation>` and assert that the seam checker refuses it.
issues.title: Workflow seam accepts a conditionally inert shell invocation

verdict.summary:
> 🤖 SPARQ agent

The reporter's parent selection, head binding, unresolved-operand handling, and live workflow wiring are otherwise coherent, but the structural guard advertised as preventing a silently vacuous report does not establish that the shell actually executes the invocation. Because this is the stated non-vacuity control for an always-zero advisory, the gap is major and approval would be unsound.
